phase3_findings.description: The two new assertions match only the literal prefix `run-parallel: elapsed ` (trailing space). Because the printf renders the value followed by a literal `s`, the pattern also matches `run-parallel: elapsed s` (empty $SECONDS), so neither assertion pins that the emitted value is a non-empty non-negative integer. The sub-one-second lower-bound case the issue's testing strategy names (PSR_T6 completes in <1s, so $SECONDS is 0) is exercised but not asserted — no case pins that a sub-second run renders `elapsed 0s`. A regression breaking the value expansion would pass both tests. (Also covers the clean-path assertion at lines 667-671.)
phase3_findings.over_grade_flag: shape 3 — uncorroborated single-source from pr-test-analyzer; observable fail-direction is a test-tightness gap, not a runtime defect. $SECONDS is a bash builtin that cannot be empty, so the empty-value case is theoretical. Advisory only; does not change the verdict.

phase3_findings.description: The added two-line comment above the elapsed printf mixes a prevention clause ("placed before the AGGREGATE_RC branch below so the branch cannot skip it", which names a concrete wrong change) with a derivation/justification clause ("SECONDS is a bash builtin counting from process start, so no program outside the set (AC2)"). The second clause is derivation/provenance rather than a specific wrong change a competent agent would otherwise make at that line, which brings it under the prevention-only comment standard (CLAUDE.md / phase-2-sweeps-contract §2.3). Grade: Suggestion.
